title: Why Krishna was born
hookLine: a wedding, a brother with a sword, and the reason the Lord chooses to be born
carry: avatara: God comes down when dharma falls
tomorrow: how do you hide a baby from a king who's watching?

cards: The wedding is over and the music is still playing. Devaki, a princess of the Yadu clan, has just married Vasudeva.
Her cousin Kamsa, a prince of Mathura, wants to honor her, so he takes the reins and drives the bridal chariot himself. Conches, drums, gifts of horses and elephants. A happy brother on a happy day.
Then, the Bhagavata says, a voice speaks out of the sky, without a body, straight at the driver. Fool. The eighth child of the woman you are driving will kill you.

teach.b: Kamsa grabs his cousin by the hair and draws his sword. The procession stops dead. Vasudeva doesn't fight.
He talks, gently. Death comes to everyone who is born, he says, today or in a hundred years. Killing your own sister on her wedding day won't change that.
So Vasudeva makes a terrible bargain to save her life right now: I'll bring you every son she bears. Kamsa knows Vasudeva keeps his word, and lowers the sword.

And Vasudeva does keep it: when their first son is born, he carries the baby to Kamsa himself. Before long, Kamsa locks them both in a prison and begins to kill their children. So why is this eighth child coming at all?
The Bhagavata opens the book a step earlier.

teach.h: THE EARTH, IN TEARS, ASKS FOR HELP
teach.b: The Earth, weighed down by cruel kings and their armies, takes the form of a cow and goes in tears to Brahma.
Brahma takes the gods to the shore of the ocean of milk to pray, and in his meditation the Lord's answer comes: I will be born, in Vasudeva's house. Hindus call this avatara, a descent.
In the Gita, Krishna says it himself: whenever dharma fails, I come, age after age, to protect the good. That's what Janmashtami celebrates.

teach.h: AVATARA: GOD COMES DOWN WHEN DHARMA FALLS
teach.b: As many devotees put it, not a god who stays far away, but one who comes down into the mess, and whose story starts in a prison cell.

how: The story of Krishna's birth is told in the tenth book of the Bhagavata Purana; Hindus hear it in recitations and festival retellings, especially around Janmashtami, the festival of Krishna's birth. The Gita's verses on why the Lord comes, age after age, are among its most often recited.

s: Vasudeva fights Kamsa to save Devaki
he reasons with him, then makes a promise to save her life.
in the Bhagavata, Krishna's coming begins with the Earth asking for help
burdened by cruel kings, she goes to Brahma as a cow, and the Lord promises to be born.
the warning says Devaki's first child will kill Kamsa
the voice says the eighth child.

games.q: you're Vasudeva. your bride's cousin has a sword at her throat on your wedding day. what do you do?
o: fight him with your bare hands.
reason with him, then promise him your sons.
games.why: he argues first that death comes to all, then promises every son to save Devaki's life, and he keeps the promise, even to Kamsa.

practice: Take a pen and a scrap of paper. Write down one place, in the world or in your own life, that feels heavy right now, the way the Earth felt. Under it, write in your own words the Gita's promise: whenever dharma fails, I come.
If you pray, read it back as a prayer for that place. If you don't, let it name what you hope for there. Keep the paper somewhere you'll see it.

wordCard.voice: The birth. Krishna's story starts before he is born, with the Earth's plea, a voice at a wedding, and a promise Vasudeva keeps.

orig.note: janma: birth. the Bhagavata's account of Krishna's birth begins with this wedding.
